result.title: Synthetic Augmentation for Data-Scarce Object Detection: Allocation, Dose, and Filtering Across Six Datasets
result.comment: 8 pages, 2 figures. Submitted to European Robotics Forum 2027
result.summary: Robotic perception for capturing uncooperative orbital objects and inspecting variable industrial products must often operate with limited labelled imagery. We examine a modular synthetic-augmentation pipeline, evaluating generation planning and post-generation filtering as separate interventions, with computational cost as a design constraint. Across six object-detection datasets, FLUX.1-Fill with class-specific LoRA adaptation produced dataset-dependent dose effects; the validation-selected augmentation improved mAP@50:95 on four datasets and reduced it on two. Filtering did not yield consistent gains, and FID, KID, precision, recall, and LPIPS did not consistently track detector changes. The results do not establish that image quality alone identifies useful samples. They motivate standardised evaluation and inexpensive candidate-utility measures that could identify useful samples before detector retraining, reducing repeated training cost.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在六个目标检测数据集上评估模块化合成数据增强流程，把生成规划与生成后过滤作为两种独立干预，并以计算成本为约束，发现剂量效应随数据集而异、过滤未带来稳定提升，且 FID、KID 等图像质量指标与检测器性能变化不一致。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心问题「廉价候选效用度量能否在重新训练前预测样本价值、质量指标为何与任务收益脱节」可能启发对 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、监督与贡献分配以及 latent 代理指标有效性的核查。
